## Assembly
Make and cd to flye, then make symbolic link to bbd read data using "ln -s /pvol/data/metagenome_assembly/bbd_0.1.fastq.gz ."

Make shell script in flye directory and submit job

## Binning with metabat
Create new directory metabat from the top and cd

Extract depth information
'''bash
cat ../flye/bbd/assembly_info.txt  | grep -v '#' | awk '{OFS="\t";print $1,$3}' > depths_bbd.txt
'''
Reorder contigs based on depth
'''bash
cat depths_bbd.txt | awk '{print $1}' | xargs samtools faidx ../bbd/assembly.fasta > assembly_bbd_ordered.fasta
'''
Run metabat
'''metabat2 -i assembly_bbd_ordered.fasta -a depths_bbd.txt --cvExt -o bins_bbd/metabat --seed 5
'''

## Check bin quality with checkm
mkdir and cd to checkm

Need to find the number of your largest contig in the bbd assembly.
Use this to display the lengths of all contigs sorted from shortest to longest
'''bash
cat ../bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n
'''
then run code
'''bash
mkdir bins_bbd
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/
samtools faidx ../bbd/assembly.fasta contig_120 > bins_bbd/contig_120.fa
'''
Create slurm script and submit checkm job

## Select bins based on checkm results
View results from checkm analysis using 'head checkm_results_bbd.txt'
add '-n 20' between 'head' and 'checkm...'

Extract bins with acompleteness greater than 15%
'''bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15'
'''
To extract strictly bin IDs
'''bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}'
'''

Send output to a file
'''bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt
'''

## Perform taxonomic classification with gtdbtk
mkdir and cd gtdbtk
mkdir genomes

First get while loop working

Turn this bin name into a path specifying the fasta file for the bin. So for every bin we need to prepend the path to its folder ../metabat/bins_bbd/ and append the file extension .fa

Now perform the copy

Check that it worked by listing files within genomes directory - should see one file for each of the bins

Create shell script and submit job

## Find and annotate genes with prokka
mkdir and cd prokka

Find first bin ID on list
Use first bin ID for this code
'''bash
bin=metabat.5
prokka --outdir $bin --prefix $bin  ../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa
'''

Contents of the metabat.63 folder: metabat.63.err  metabat.63.fna  metabat.63.gff  metabat.63.tbl
metabat.63.faa  metabat.63.fsa  metabat.63.log  metabat.63.tsv
metabat.63.ffn  metabat.63.gbk  metabat.63.sqn  metabat.63.txt

Want to focus on tab separated file with name of each gene and its inferred name and functional info (tsv file)

## Infer metabolic pathways
mkdir and cd minpath

Inputs for minpath will be prepared for each bin based on the prokka. look at tsv file for a single bin 
'''bash
head ../prokka/metabat.63/metabat.63.tsv
'''
9 genes displayed from this 
locus_tag       ftype   length_bp       gene    EC_number       COG     product
EFNKBEDD_00001  CDS     150                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00002  CDS     672                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00003  CDS     339                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00004  CDS     438                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00005  CDS     297                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00006  CDS     756                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00007  CDS     501                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00008  CDS     723                             hypothetical protein
EFNKBEDD_00009  CDS     276                             hypothetical protein

Transform tsv file into the format of keeping a unique ID for each gene and its EC number by using awk
'''bash
head ../prokka/metabat.63/metabat.63.tsv | awk -F '\t' '{print $1,$5}'
'''
leaving us with: EFNKBEDD_00001 
EFNKBEDD_00002 
EFNKBEDD_00003 
EFNKBEDD_00004 
EFNKBEDD_00005 
EFNKBEDD_00006 
EFNKBEDD_00007 
EFNKBEDD_00008 
EFNKBEDD_00009 

Remove header line and ensure output is tab separated
'''bash
head ../prokka/metabat.63/metabat.63.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'
'''
The first 10 lines did not have EC numbers, so have to check top 50
To include all genes, change head to cat

Send output to a file so it can be used as input to minpath
'''bash
cat ../prokka/metabat.63/metabat.63.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.63.ec
'''

Run minpath on this file: minpath -ec metabat.63.ec -report metabat.63.ec.report -details metabat.63.ec.details
This creates a report

Consider first line of output:
path PWY-7321 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 1  fam0  4  fam-found  2  name  ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods)

Prepare minpath inputs for all bins
